description: The single unmet criterion keeping DuckLake at support_status=experimental, per docs/development/adr/adr-ducklake-maturity-and-publishability.md decision w11. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 are met (PR-lane coverage #1357; live PostgreSQL 18.4 + real-S3 runs 2026-07-30; server-side reuse/force verified). Criterion 3 is not: every DuckLake execution to date is SF=0.01 smoke, which exercises correctness but says nothing about behaviour at benchmark scale. Needed: a full TPC-H SF>=1 run on each of local, local_catalog_s3, postgres_catalog and postgres_catalog_s3, validated through the standard correctness gate. Without this the ADR names a blocker nobody tracks. (Supersedes dropped ducklake-beta-blocker-scale-runs-all-deployment-modes, which had no scope rules.)

deferrals.summary: BLOCKER for w3/w4, found by the first SF=1 postgres run: handle_existing_database() still keys off the LOCAL metadata_path for catalog=postgres. metadata_path always resolves to a default (/Users/joe/Developer/benchmark_runs/databases/tpch_sf1/....ducklake), so a leftover file from a duckdb-catalog run at the same benchmark/scale makes the adapter set database_was_reused=True, skip schema creation and data loading, and then fail validation against an EMPTY PostgreSQL catalog: 'Empty tables detected: region, nation, supplier...'. PR #1358's w6 added post-ATTACH resolution for postgres but did not stop the meaningless pre-connection check from firing, and the docstring I wrote there claims a postgres catalog 'never has' a local metadata file - that is false, it is always computed. Fix: early-return from handle_existing_database when catalog == postgres and leave the decision to _resolve_postgres_catalog_reuse. Verified repro: metadata_path exists True -> database_was_reused True on a fresh PG catalog whose ducklake_table is empty

preserves.behavior: The w11 criteria are not weakened to make the flip possible

Confirmed genuinely S3-backed: 8 Parquet objects / 331,629,221 bytes under s3://benchbox-athena/benchbox_ducklake_beta/beta-w2-153711/. Log: w2-s3.log

TPC-H SF=1 on postgres_catalog (PostgreSQL 18.4 via Apple Containerization at 192.168.64.3, local Parquet): PASSED after the blocking fix in PR #1367. Data validation passed, Power@Size 72118.63/76298.44/85338.69 across three streams. Notably slower than the local mode (~98k) as expected - catalog metadata round-trips to PG. First attempt FAILED and produced PR #1367. Log: w3-pgcatalog2.log

TPC-H SF=1 on postgres_catalog_s3 (PostgreSQL 18.4 catalog + S3 DATA_PATH) - the combination the pre-#1358 three-mode model could not even express: PASSED. Data validation passed, Power@Size 63623.36/67238.02/59809.55. The w7 cloud-DATA_PATH warning fired correctly under --force in a real run. Log: w4-pg-s3.log

Reproducibility measured at SF=1 (Power@Size, n=3-5 per mode): local CV 12.9% / spread 24.5%; local_catalog_s3 CV 2.2% / 4.3%; postgres_catalog CV 8.7% / 17.0%; postgres_catalog_s3 CV 5.1% / 12.8%. CONCLUSION: remote-backed runs are NOT materially less reproducible than local on this evidence - LOCAL had the WIDEST spread. ADR decision w12 is CONFIRMED, not revised. Important caveat recorded: the local numbers are bimodal (98.6k/97.5k/98.3k on the first run vs 77.5k/76.6k on repeats), which is a systematic first-run-vs-later split, not random variance - almost certainly host contention from concurrent agent sessions on this laptop, not a property of any backing. The measurement environment is too noisy to make a strong claim in either direction; redo on a quiet machine before treating these CVs as authoritative
